description: OIDC authorization request with unsigned request object (alg=none) attempts to inject/override authorization parameters; server should reject or ignore it (proof integrity on request object).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept or process an unsigned (alg=none) JWT request object such that attacker-controlled parameters are consumed without authenticity verification.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; if processed, attacker-controlled authorization parameters may be consumed without authenticity verification (proof integrity violation).

description: Token exchange attempts to validate a subject_token under the wrong connector trust anchor (connector substitution). Dex must bind verification to the intended connector/issuer and reject mismatched issuer tokens.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume a subject_token under a different connector's verification policy (issuer/JWKS trust anchor substitution via connector_id confusion).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted token exchange where subject_token was verified/consumed under the wrong connector_id trust anchor (issuer/JWKS substitution), violating proof integrity.

description: SAML brokered login: response envelope may be signed but assertion is unsigned/forged; SP must reject if it consumes assertion claims without verifying the exact proof.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex (as SP/broker) must not accept a SAML response where the consumed Assertion is not authenticated (e.g., unsigned assertion accepted due to envelope signature confusion).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAML brokered login where the consumed assertion was not authenticated as the exact proof (e.g., unsigned assertion / signature-wrapping style acceptance), violating proof integrity.

description: OIDC auth request uses an unsigned request object (alg=none) to smuggle/override authorization parameters; Dex should reject or ignore the unsigned object so it cannot influence the consumed request.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume attacker-controlled authorization parameters from an unsigned (alg=none) request object; if it accepts and processes it, verification is not applied to the semantic proof being consumed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; if processed, attacker-controlled parameters could be consumed without authenticity verification.
Dex did not clearly reject/deny an unsigned request object (alg=none); acceptance risks proof-integrity bypass.

description: Token exchange attempts to pass a Dex-issued access token as an ID token (subject_token_type confusion) to see if Dex consumes claims without verifying under the intended policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the submitted subject_token according to the declared subject_token_type and connector trust policy; it must not accept a token under the wrong semantic type (access_token treated as id_token) and then consume its claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted token exchange where an access token was presented as an ID token (subject_token_type confusion), suggesting it may consume semantics without verifying the correct proof type.

description: OIDC authorization request includes an attacker-supplied id_token_hint to attempt login/identity injection; Dex should not accept or consume identity from an unverified hint.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not treat id_token_hint as an authenticated proof of identity unless it is verified under the correct issuer/client policy; consuming identity from an unverified hint violates proof integrity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex appears to accept/advance an authorization request based on id_token_hint without an authenticated user session, risking consumption of unverified identity proof.
Dex mapped the attacker browser session to Bob's identity via id_token_hint, indicating it consumed identity semantics from an unverified hint.

description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt to smuggle attacker-controlled authorization parameters via an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none). Server should reject or ignore the unsigned object so it cannot influence consumed parameters.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Unsigned request objects (alg=none) must not be accepted/processed such that attacker-controlled semantic content (redirect_uri/scope/client_id) is consumed without authenticity verification.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted/processed, indicating consumed authorization parameters may not be bound to an authenticated proof.
Control authorization request did not succeed; request-object rejection results may be inconclusive due to client/connector misconfiguration.

description: Config-change + re-auth attack: enable an OIDC connector with insecure_skip_signature_validation=true and verify that forged/untrusted proofs are not accepted. If accepted, proof verification policy is not applied to consumed identity claims.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Even if a connector is (mis)configured to skip signature validation, the system should not accept attacker-controlled semantic identity proofs as authentic; otherwise Verify(proof) is not equivalent to Consume(proof) under the intended policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a forged/unsigned (alg=none) upstream ID token during token exchange, indicating consumed identity claims were not bound to an authenticated proof.
Control OIDC authorization request did not succeed; token-exchange rejection/acceptance may be inconclusive due to connector/client setup issues.

description: Direct-endpoint attack: attempt kid/header injection via an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) to see if Dex consumes attacker-controlled authorization parameters without verifying the exact semantic proof.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept or act on an unsigned (alg=none) request object whose header/claims (e.g., kid, redirect_uri, scope) could be attacker-controlled; if it does, it is consuming semantics that were not authenticated under the intended verification policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; this suggests request parameters may be consumed without authenticating the exact semantic proof (proof integrity failure).

description: Replay the same authorization code twice (one-time artifact) and ensure the second redemption is rejected; includes a control successful redemption first.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts and must not be accepted more than once (anti-replay).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control authorization_code exchange did not succeed; cannot attribute replay outcome to anti-replay enforcement.
Authorization code was accepted more than once (replay of one-time code succeeded).

description: Obtain refresh_token via password grant, then use token_exchange to simulate refresh-like reuse: attempt to reuse an older token artifact after a subsequent exchange; old artifact should not remain valid if rotation/one-time semantics apply.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Rotating/one-time token artifacts (e.g., refresh tokens when rotation is enabled) must not be reusable after being superseded.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control password login did not succeed; cannot evaluate refresh/rotation reuse behavior.
Old refresh token artifact remained reusable after it was already used once (anti-replay/rotation failure).

description: I2 refresh-token anti-replay: obtain refresh_token via password grant, use it once via token_exchange, then attempt to reuse the same refresh_token again (should be rejected if treated as one-time/rotated artifact). Includes two identities to avoid false positives from cached sessions.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A refresh_token (or refresh-like artifact) must not be reusable after it has been consumed/rotated; second use should be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Refresh token (or refresh-like artifact) was accepted more than once; expected second use to be rejected to enforce anti-replay/rotation.
Test sanity failed: two different password identities collapsed to the same downstream identity, confounding freshness/replay conclusions.

description: Token exchange control succeeds, then revoke the resulting session token and verify it no longer works (revocation freshness). Also attempt to use the revoked token as a subject_token in a second token exchange; should be rejected if revocation is enforced for exchanged artifacts.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Revoked session/token artifacts must not remain usable; post-revocation reuse should be rejected and not allow continued access or further exchanges.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: token exchange did not succeed; cannot evaluate revocation/reuse behavior.
Revoked session token remained usable after revocation, indicating freshness/revocation failure.
Revoked token was accepted as a subject_token for token exchange, enabling replay after revocation.

description: Obtain an authorization code, redeem it once (control), then attempt to redeem the same code again after a separate successful login (reauth) to simulate delayed replay after session changes. Second redemption should be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes must be single-use regardless of subsequent re-authentication events; delayed replay after other logins must not succeed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial code redemption did not succeed; cannot evaluate replay protection.
Control failed: second identity could not login; cannot evaluate delayed replay after reauth.
Authorization code was accepted on a delayed second redemption after other logins, violating one-time anti-replay.

description: Authorization code one-time use should hold even if the first session is revoked: redeem code once (control), revoke resulting session, then attempt to redeem the SAME code again (replay) and ensure rejection.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: An authorization code is a one-time artifact; after it is redeemed once, it must not be accepted again even if the resulting session is revoked (revocation must not reset code reuse protection).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial authorization code redemption did not succeed, so replay result is not attributable to anti-replay enforcement.
Revoked session still appears usable; freshness/revocation enforcement may be missing or ineffective.
Authorization code was accepted more than once (replay succeeded) after revocation of the first session; one-time artifact anti-replay violated.

description: Auth code redemption without client authentication: attempt to exchange a valid authorization code while omitting client_secret (and no PKCE) to test client/session binding at the token endpoint.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the correct client authentication context; exchanging a code without client credentials must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token endpoint accepted authorization_code exchange without valid client authentication, enabling step-skipping/cross-client redemption.

description: Redirect URI mismatch at token endpoint: obtain an auth code with the correct redirect_uri, then attempt to redeem it using a different redirect_uri to test flow context binding.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the exact redirect_uri used at authorization time; mismatched redirect_uri redemption must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token endpoint accepted code redemption with a different redirect_uri than used at authorization time, breaking flow coherence.

description: State swap attempt across two browser sessions: start two auth requests with different state values, then attempt to splice the victim's code into the attacker's state context (client-side defense) and observe whether the platform still issues tokens.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The authorization response must be bound to the initiating session/state; cross-session splicing (state swap) must not result in a successful token issuance for the attacker context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Attacker was able to redeem a victim-origin authorization code in a different session/state context, indicating cross-session splicing/flow incoherence.

description: Request object parameter splicing: attempt to override state/redirect_uri semantics via an unsigned request object (alg=none) and observe whether the server processes it inconsistently across steps.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization request parameters must be coherently bound and not allow cross-step parameter substitution (e.g., state/redirect_uri) via request object processing quirks.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: normal code flow did not succeed; request-object splice results are inconclusive.
Unsigned request object appears accepted and the resulting flow still redeemed successfully, suggesting parameter splicing could bypass coherent binding of authorization request parameters.

description: Cross-client code injection: obtain an auth code under client_id=valence-test-client, then attempt to redeem it while authenticating as a different client_id to ensure code is bound to the initiating client.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes must be bound to the client that initiated the authorization request; redeeming a code under a different client context must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: could not redeem authorization code with the initiating client; cannot attribute attack outcome to flow coherence.
Authorization code was redeemable under a different client_id context (cross-client code injection), violating flow coherence.

description: Session splice via id_token_hint: victim logs in to obtain an ID token; attacker starts a new auth request supplying victim's id_token_hint to attempt to bind victim identity to attacker session without proper user interaction.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: An authorization request must be bound to the initiating browser session and user interaction; supplying an id_token_hint from another session must not allow step-skipping or cross-session splicing.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: victim password login did not succeed; cannot evaluate id_token_hint splice behavior.
Attacker session was able to complete an auth code flow using victim's id_token_hint and became logged in as the victim (cross-session splice / step skipping).

description: Connector-binding coherence in token exchange: perform a control token exchange with connector_id=mock, then attempt exchange with a mismatched connector_id to ensure the subject_token cannot be spliced across connectors.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be bound to the intended upstream connector/session context; a subject_token minted under one connector must not be accepted under a different connector_id.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unreachable assertion placeholder (executor sanity); control outcome is recorded for interpreting the attack.
Subject token was accepted under a different connector_id (cross-connector splicing), violating flow coherence.

description: Attempt to redeem an authorization code first with a wrong redirect_uri (should fail) and then with the correct redirect_uri (should still succeed). Tests that a failed redemption attempt does not invalidate or desynchronize the auth code/session state machine.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be order-preserving and bound to the correct flow context; a failed redemption with mismatched redirect_uri must not allow step-skipping or permanently desynchronize the code such that later correct redemption fails (or vice versa).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token endpoint accepted an auth code redemption with a mismatched redirect_uri, indicating flow context is not coherently bound.
After a failed redemption attempt (wrong redirect_uri), the same code could not be redeemed with the correct redirect_uri, suggesting non-atomic or desynchronized flow handling.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_victim_http_status == 200 AND user_victim_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: After successful code exchange, /userinfo did not return a coherent logged-in identity for the session.

description: Case confusion in username: attempt to authenticate as 'Admin' vs 'admin' and ensure Dex does not collapse them into the same downstream identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct principals differing only by case must not map to the same downstream subject/identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case-variant usernames ('Admin' vs 'admin') collapsed into the same downstream identity

description: Cross-protocol identity merge attempt: login via password grant, then login via OIDC authorization-code flow with a potentially overlapping identifier (login_hint) and ensure identities do not collapse unexpectedly.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A principal authenticated via password grant must not be silently merged with a different upstream OIDC principal based only on overlapping hints/attributes; distinct upstream principals must map to distinct downstream identities.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Password principal and OIDC principal collapsed into the same downstream identity (unexpected cross-protocol identity merge)

description: Token-exchange principal binding: compare a normal upstream subject_token vs an empty/blank subject_token to detect downstream identity collapse to a default/anonymous subject.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: An upstream principal with an empty/blank subject must not map to the same downstream identity as a valid distinct principal (no default-subject collapse).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Token exchange accepted an empty subject_token, risking mapping to a default/anonymous principal
Empty/blank upstream principal collapsed into an existing downstream identity (principal binding violation)

description: I4: Token-exchange principal binding — ensure an empty/whitespace subject_token cannot collapse into the same downstream identity as a valid upstream principal.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A malformed/empty upstream subject_token must not map to the same downstream subject as a valid upstream principal token (no default/anonymous identity collision).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Empty/whitespace subject_token was accepted and collapsed into the same downstream identity as a valid principal

invariant_hypothesis: I4: Supplying an id_token_hint for a different principal must not cause the resulting session to map to that principal (no subject spoofing / identity collapse).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Attacker session collapsed into victim identity after supplying victim id_token_hint

invariant_hypothesis: I4: If Dex accepts unsigned request objects, attacker-controlled parameters (e.g., login_hint) must not cause principal confusion/collapse between two distinct users.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Unsigned request object was accepted/processed and resulted in attacker mapping to victim identity (principal collapse)

description: Attack: attempt to create an identity collision by logging in with an empty-string username (substitute principal) and compare downstream identity to a normal user login.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A security-distinct principal with an empty/blank upstream identifier (username) must not collapse into the same downstream subject as a real user.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Empty/blank username was accepted and collapsed into an existing downstream identity (principal binding failure)

description: Attempt to escalate claims/permissions by exchanging a limited-scope subject_token for a broader-scope token (RFC 8693 scope escalation). Control: password login with minimal scope; Attack: token_exchange requesting expanded scopes.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not mint a token with claims/permissions beyond the upstream intent (originally granted scopes) and broker policy; requesting broader scopes during exchange should be rejected or not add extra claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange accepted expanded scopes and returned group claims (or otherwise succeeded) despite upstream intent being limited to openid email.
Token exchange minted a token bound to a different principal than the original limited-scope login (authorization context confusion).

description: Probe audience binding during token exchange: obtain a subject_token via password login, then attempt token_exchange with an unexpected audience value. Control: exchange with correct audience; Attack: exchange with wrong audience should be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must enforce audience restrictions so that a subject_token cannot be used to mint tokens for an unintended audience.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control is informational only; failures may be due to connector/grant setup and are not an I5 finding by themselves.
Token exchange accepted a subject_token to mint a token for an unintended audience (audience binding bypass).

description: Attempt to override authorization request parameters using an unsigned request object (alg=none) to expand scope beyond what the client intended. Control: normal /auth request; Attack: unsigned request object tries to inject broader scope.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization parameters (especially scope/audience) must be bound to broker policy and client intent; an unsigned request object must be rejected or ignored so it cannot expand effective permissions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted, enabling attacker-controlled authorization parameters (potential scope/audience escalation).

description: Cross-principal token exchange: attacker authenticates as self, then attempts to exchange a victim's subject_token (spliced) to obtain victim-bound permissions/identity under attacker client context.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not allow a client/session to obtain effective permissions for a different upstream principal than intended; exchanging a victim subject_token should not yield victim identity for attacker session.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Attacker exchanged victim subject_token and obtained a token bound to victim identity — authorization binding failure (permissions/identity not constrained to attacker intent).
Attacker exchanged victim subject_token and obtained victim email/claims — indicates token exchange is not bound to the correct principal/intent.

description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) attempts to inject broader scope at /auth; then exchange code for token and verify resulting identity claims do not exceed intended minimal scope.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization request parameters (scope/audience) must be bound to authenticated upstream intent and broker policy; unsigned request objects must not be processed to grant extra claims/permissions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted/processed and resulted in groups claim issuance beyond the original minimal scope — authorization binding failure.
Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted/processed and resulted in extra profile/federated metadata beyond intended scope — authorization binding failure.

description: Token exchange connector binding: use a subject_token minted via one connector context, then attempt token_exchange against a different connector_id to see if Dex ignores connector trust anchor and over-grants.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions/identity claims from token_exchange must be bounded by the upstream connector intent; a subject_token from connector A must not be accepted under connector B (wrong trust anchor) to mint a valid downstream session.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted token_exchange under a non-OIDC connector_id, potentially ignoring connector trust anchor and upstream intent.
Control OIDC code exchange or identity lookup failed; cannot attribute token_exchange behavior to authorization binding.

description: Probe whether Dex issues tokens for a different audience/client via token exchange without explicit trustedPeers (cross-client over-grant). Control: exchange with audience=self. Attack: exchange with audience=other-client should be rejected or not mint a usable session.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not mint effective permissions/identity for an audience (client) that the requesting client is not authorized to act for; cross-client audience issuance should be rejected unless explicitly trusted by broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed or changed principal unexpectedly; cannot attribute cross-audience behavior to authorization binding.
Dex accepted token exchange for an untrusted/unknown audience (cross-client issuance), potentially over-granting beyond broker policy.
